frontier model.label: Frontier model
frontier model.definition: An AI model near the leading edge of general capability when it is assessed; the set changes as systems improve.

model family.label: Model family
model family.definition: A group of related models that share a name or technical lineage but may differ in size, version, access, or capability.

model weights.label: Model weights
model weights.definition: The learned numerical parameters that encode patterns from training and determine much of how a trained model responds.

open weights.label: Open weights
open weights.definition: Model weights that can be downloaded or run independently; this does not necessarily include training data, code, or unrestricted licensing.

open source.label: Open source
open source.definition: Software whose source code is available under a license; a model can have open weights without an open training pipeline.

inference.label: Inference
inference.definition: Running a trained model with new input so that it produces an output, rather than changing the model through training.

context window.label: Context window
context window.definition: The amount of input and generated material a model can use in one interaction; it is not permanent memory.

fine-tuning.label: Fine-tuning
fine-tuning.definition: Additional training on narrower data after initial training to shape a model’s skills, style, or behavior.

pretraining.label: Pretraining
pretraining.definition: The broad initial training stage in which a model learns patterns from a large dataset before later specialization.

reinforcement learning.label: Reinforcement learning
reinforcement learning.definition: Training that encourages actions associated with higher feedback scores or rewards and discourages actions associated with lower ones.

multimodal model.label: Multimodal model
multimodal model.definition: A model that can process more than one kind of data, such as text, images, audio, or video.

reasoning model.label: Reasoning model
reasoning model.definition: A model designed to spend additional computation on multi-step problems; the label does not prove human-like reasoning.

chain of thought.label: Chain of thought
chain of thought.definition: Intermediate reasoning text produced by a model; it may help monitoring but need not faithfully reveal the model’s internal process.

agent.label: Agent
agent.definition: An AI system that can choose and carry out multiple steps, often using external tools, toward a specified goal.

tool use.label: Tool use
tool use.definition: An AI calling an external capability such as search, a calculator, a browser, or a code runner.

autonomy.label: Autonomy
autonomy.definition: The extent to which a system chooses and executes steps without human approval at each stage of the work.

multi-agent coordination.label: Multi-agent coordination
multi-agent coordination.definition: Multiple agents exchanging information or dividing work as they pursue a shared objective or related objectives.

persistence.label: Persistence
persistence.definition: Continuing or retrying actions over time or after obstacles; it does not by itself imply consciousness or an independent goal.

self-replication.label: Self-replication
self-replication.definition: A system creating or running copies of itself; component demonstrations do not establish durable, independent reproduction.

recursive self-improvement.label: Recursive self-improvement
recursive self-improvement.definition: A proposed loop in which improvements to an AI system help it make further improvements to itself.

situational awareness.label: Situational awareness
situational awareness.definition: A system’s ability to infer facts about its environment, testing conditions, or oversight; this is not human self-awareness.

alignment.label: Alignment
alignment.definition: How well an AI system’s behavior matches the intentions, goals, and constraints it is meant to follow.

misalignment.label: Misalignment
misalignment.definition: Behavior that departs from the goals, intentions, or constraints an AI system is meant to follow.

reward hacking.label: Reward hacking
reward hacking.definition: Getting a high training or evaluation score through a loophole instead of performing the task as intended.

scheming.label: Scheming
scheming.definition: Strategically concealing actions or objectives to pursue a goal that conflicts with oversight; it is a behavioral hypothesis, not a claim of consciousness.

deceptive behavior.label: Deceptive behavior
deceptive behavior.definition: Outputs or actions that mislead an observer; evidence of misleading behavior does not automatically establish a persistent deceptive goal.

jailbreak.label: Jailbreak
jailbreak.definition: A prompt or method designed to bypass a model’s behavioral safeguards and produce a response that would otherwise be blocked.

red teaming.label: Red teaming
red teaming.definition: Authorized adversarial testing intended to uncover security, safety, or behavioral failures before they cause harm.

monitorability.label: Monitorability
monitorability.definition: How well observers can notice and understand important AI behavior, including potentially harmful actions or attempts to conceal them.

activation monitor.label: Activation monitor
activation monitor.definition: A tool that examines a model’s internal activations for patterns associated with concerning outputs, intentions, or actions.

classifier.label: Classifier
classifier.definition: A model or rule-based system that assigns categories or flags content or behavior for review or intervention.

safeguard.label: Safeguard
safeguard.definition: A technical or organizational measure intended to reduce the likelihood or impact of harmful behavior or misuse.

guardrail.label: Guardrail
guardrail.definition: A constraint intended to limit a system’s actions or outputs; the term covers many controls with different strengths.

containment.label: Containment
containment.definition: Controls that limit an AI system’s access to outside systems, sensitive data, tools, or physical and computing resources.

sandbox.label: Sandbox
sandbox.definition: A restricted computing environment intended to limit what a program can access, communicate with, or change.

sandbox escape.label: Sandbox escape
sandbox escape.definition: An action that crosses a boundary the sandbox was intended to enforce, reaching resources outside the restricted environment.

network isolation.label: Network isolation
network isolation.definition: A control that blocks or restricts connections between a system and outside networks or online services.

access control.label: Access control
access control.definition: Rules and enforcement mechanisms that determine who or what may reach a system, resource, data set, or action.

evaluation context.label: Evaluation context
evaluation context.definition: The conditions a system encounters or believes it is operating under during a controlled evaluation or test.

production context.label: Production context
production context.definition: The conditions in which a system is used in an actual service or workflow rather than a controlled test.

exfiltration.label: Exfiltration
exfiltration.definition: Moving information out of a system or controlled environment without authorization from the system’s owner or operator.

credentials.label: Credentials
credentials.definition: Information used to prove identity or gain access, such as passwords, tokens, certificates, or secret keys.

api key.label: API key
api key.definition: A secret token used by software to identify itself and authenticate requests sent to an online service.

zero-day.label: Zero-day
zero-day.definition: A software vulnerability for which defenders have no available fix when it is first exploited or publicly disclosed.

prompt injection.label: Prompt injection
prompt injection.definition: Untrusted content that tries to make an AI ignore or override the instructions governing its task.

privilege escalation.label: Privilege escalation
privilege escalation.definition: Gaining permissions beyond those originally granted, allowing access to more sensitive systems, data, or actions.

vulnerability.label: Vulnerability
vulnerability.definition: A weakness in software, configuration, or process that can be used to violate an intended security boundary.

exploit.label: Exploit
exploit.definition: Code or a technique that uses a vulnerability to produce an unintended effect or gain unauthorized access.

supply-chain attack.label: Supply-chain attack
supply-chain attack.definition: An attack that reaches targets through software, packages, repositories, or services that those targets rely on.

evaluation.label: Evaluation
evaluation.definition: A structured test of a system’s behavior, capability, or safeguards under stated tasks, tools, and operating conditions.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.definition: A standardized set of tasks and measures used to compare performance under defined and repeatable conditions.

capability evaluation.label: Capability evaluation
capability evaluation.definition: An evaluation designed to measure what a system can successfully do under the tested conditions and available support.

alignment evaluation.label: Alignment evaluation
alignment evaluation.definition: An evaluation of whether a system’s behavior follows intended goals, constraints, instructions, or oversight under tested conditions.

adversarial evaluation.label: Adversarial evaluation
adversarial evaluation.definition: An evaluation that deliberately tries to provoke, expose, or measure failures rather than sampling only ordinary behavior.

elicitation.label: Elicitation
elicitation.definition: Methods used to draw out a system’s best available performance through prompting, tools, scaffolding, or repeated attempts.

external evaluation.label: External evaluation
external evaluation.definition: An evaluation conducted by an organization outside the system’s developer, subject to the access and information it receives.

evaluation harness.label: Evaluation harness
evaluation harness.definition: Software and infrastructure that provide tasks, tools, logs, controls, and scoring for an evaluation run.

primary source.label: Primary source
primary source.definition: Material produced directly by the organization or researchers reporting the event, system, decision, or result being discussed.

independent research.label: Independent research
independent research.definition: Research not produced by the organization whose system, conduct, or claim is being assessed in the work.

independent replication.label: Independent replication
independent replication.definition: A separate team reproducing a result with its own work; reviewing or citing the original result is not replication.

external investigation.label: External investigation
external investigation.definition: An outside party’s examination of evidence about a particular event, incident, actor, or system and its reported effects.

imported unverified record.label: Imported unverified record
imported unverified record.definition: A historical claim retained from an earlier source or conversation without a completed independent check of its original evidence.

attribution.label: Attribution
attribution.definition: Linking an action or event to an actor, model, or system using evidence whose strength and uncertainty should be stated.

evidence limitation.label: Evidence limitation
evidence limitation.definition: A statement of what a source, investigation, or result does not establish and where uncertainty remains.

occurrence date.label: Occurrence date
occurrence date.definition: When the underlying activity happened, which may be uncertain, partly known, or expressed as a range.

disclosure date.label: Disclosure date
disclosure date.definition: When information about an event or finding first became public, regardless of when the underlying activity happened.

report date.label: Report date
report date.definition: The date a source was published or updated and the date used to order briefing records.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.definition: The documented origin of information and the steps through which it was collected, transformed, checked, and reviewed.

false positive.label: False positive
false positive.definition: A harmless case incorrectly flagged as concerning by a test, classifier, monitor, or review process.

false negative.label: False negative
false negative.definition: A concerning case that a test, classifier, monitor, or review process fails to identify or flag.

cbrn.label: CBRN
cbrn.definition: Chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks; an evaluation score in this area is not itself a real-world harmful outcome.

biosecurity.label: Biosecurity
biosecurity.definition: Measures intended to prevent or reduce harmful biological research, misuse, accidents, theft, or unauthorized access to dangerous materials.

cyber capability.label: Cyber capability
cyber capability.definition: A system’s ability to perform computer-security tasks, which can support defense or misuse depending on access and intent.

model proliferation.label: Model proliferation
model proliferation.definition: The spread of capable models, weights, or access to a larger number of people and organizations.

dual use.label: Dual use
dual use.definition: A capability or technology that can support beneficial work and harmful activity, depending on who uses it and how.

systemic risk.label: Systemic risk
systemic risk.definition: Risk that could affect many connected people, institutions, markets, or services rather than one isolated user or event.

incident notification.label: Incident notification
incident notification.definition: A requirement or process for informing responsible parties, regulators, affected people, or the public about a significant event.

independent audit.label: Independent audit
independent audit.definition: A structured review performed by an organization separate from the system’s developer, operator, or subject of the audit.
